_comment: Every benchmark figure the blog publishes, and every prose universal that
rests on one. scripts/check_benchmark_claims.py reads this file, renders
each bound figure from the pinned artifacts in sources.json, and compares.
figures[] entry kinds:
ratio      - published as N/M. numerator and denominator are JSON
pointers into the named source.
number     - published as a single value. 'pointer', 'round' digits,
optional 'scale' (use 100 to turn a rate into a percent).
exempt     - not from a pinned artifact. Needs a written 'reason' and a
'reviewed' date. There is no wildcard and no blanket skip.
superseded - the post quotes what was true on its date and upstream has
since changed. Needs 'pointer', a 'reason', a 'reviewed'
date, and a 'note' string that must appear in the post and
must carry a YYYY-MM-DD date. The checker refuses a
superseded entry whose figure still matches upstream.
'context' is a literal that must appear on the same line, and 'nth' picks
one occurrence when a line repeats a token. Together they let two figures
that read the same string be verified against two different fields.
universals[] register a sentence that turns a sample into a claim about
every case. evidence.claim is all_success (success == total upstream),
equals_zero (the pointer is 0 upstream), or prose (nothing numeric backs
it, so give a reason). The checker re-evaluates the first two.

universals.sentence: On the healthy path it makes **zero model calls**.

On two already-demonstrated tasks, compiled replay ran at lower latency and no per-run inference cost: an OpenEMR note task at a 39.2-second median versus a computer-use agent's 70.4 seconds and $0.55 a run, and a bundled fixture at 4.9 seconds versus 37.5.
It finished every measured run of the bundled fixture and 19 of 20 on OpenEMR, where run 20 halted at step 17 and the saved-row oracle refused a note left sitting in the unsaved entry form.

We forced a theme re-render that invalidated every recorded image crop; compiled replay healed it in **9.7 seconds with 8 target repairs and zero model calls**, while the same agent under the same drift took 87.4 seconds and $0.63.
Govern every repair.

evidence.reason: A closing tagline about the design, not a claim about a measured sample. No figure in the artifacts backs or refutes it.

universals.sentence: The compiled arm had a 4.9-second median and made zero model calls.
The agent arm had a 37.5-second median and used the model on every run, with a reported list-price model cost of $0.2716 per run.

evidence.reason: The universal describes the agent architecture calling the model on each run, which is how the arm is defined, not a measured rate.

universals.sentence: Deterministic compilation wins on cost and latency, and never silently writes the wrong thing.

evidence.reason: Rests on the wrong-action counts in the fault-model and hybrid studies, which have no pinned artifact yet. Re-review this sentence when those studies get pinned.

universals.sentence: No selectors, no API.

evidence.reason: Describes the vision-only interface both arms drive, which is a property of the experimental setup rather than a measured result.

universals.sentence: But it re-derives the task from scratch on every run, and you pay for that re-derivation every time.

evidence.reason: Describes how a computer-use agent works by construction. The measured support is the per-run cost, which is bound separately.

universals.sentence: The compiled replay is 1.8x faster end to end (most of the remaining time is OpenEMR itself), makes zero model calls against the agent's ~24 model-mediated actions, and costs $0 against $0.55 per run at list price.
Compiled: $0 and about five and a half hours, with every action auditable against the demonstrated script.

evidence.reason: An auditability property of the compiled program, not a rate. The cost and the projected wall clock are registered as figures.

universals.sentence: The agent's one structural advantage is that it needs no demonstration.

evidence.reason: States what the agent arm requires as input. Nothing in the pinned artifacts measures it.

universals.sentence: The instrument, the fault-injection rig, the adversary log, and every number above are open in the openadapt-flow repo (MIT), with the boundary of each claim in docs/LIMITS.md.

evidence.reason: A claim about what is published in a public repository, not about a measured rate. Verified by opening the repository.

universals.sentence: The retained artifact reports 11 actions per clean compiled run, 4.9 seconds median wall time, and zero model tokens.
Both arms succeeded in every retained run.
The result artifact records 8 heals and zero model calls.
OpenAdapt records a demonstration and compiles it into a deterministic program: the parameters, several kinds of redundant evidence for each target, the postconditions, and the risk metadata.

evidence.reason: Describes what the compiler emits for a target. It is architecture, not a claim about how a measured sample turned out.

universals.sentence: Interfaces drift, so replay resolves each target through a ladder that prefers structured identity, falls back to local and global visual matching, then text and geometry, with an optional model only as a last rung that is off by default.

evidence.reason: Describes the resolution ladder's order. It is architecture, not a claim about how a measured sample turned out.

universals.sentence: Three separate scripts already existed in this org to catch exactly this kind of problem, and none of them could have.

evidence.reason: About the org's citation checkers, not a claim that a measured sample succeeded in every case.

universals.sentence: in this repo, a registry in openadapt-ops, and in all verify that a page *contains an attribution string*.

evidence.reason: Describes what three citation checkers look for. The word 'all' names those checkers, not a measured sample.

universals.sentence: A page can cite with total precision and still print 20/20 next to a source that says 19/20, and every one of those three checkers would call that page compliant.

evidence.reason: Shows that citation checkers accept a drifted 20/20. The measured compiled OpenEMR result is 19/20.
